_about.purpose: Hand-written evaluation corpus for Phase 3 (English / Hindi / Hinglish). Not generated — each message was written deliberately and each expected_mood was assigned by reading the message, before any model was run against it.
_about.relationship_note: StillWithYou mediates communication between any two people, not couples. Writing everything as partner-to-partner would bake in an assumed baseline of intimacy and empathy that most real conversations do not have. So these 30 span friends, roommates, siblings, classmates, colleagues and family — and the `context` field on each entry records which, so a later reader can check the spread rather than trust it.
_about.distinctness_note: All 30 messages are different. An earlier draft of this file was 10 messages rendered in three languages; that measures translation consistency, not per-language accuracy, and it lets one badly-chosen message skew all three categories at once.
_about.register_note: The Hinglish entries use the compressed spellings people actually type — nhi, h, rhi, mai, gyi, rha, kr, bhut — not textbook transliteration. Clean Hinglish would flatter the Step 3 detector against input it will never see.
_about.balance_note: 15 per language: 3 calm, 3 neutral, 4 frustrated, 5 angry. An earlier draft had n=2 for frustrated and angry, where a single wrong call moves a category accuracy by 50 points — closer to noise than measurement, in exactly the two categories this product exists to detect.
_about.lexicon_independence_note: Items 11-15 in each language are deliberately free of every term in the analyzer's own escalation lexicon (pathetic, stupid, useless, बकवास, बेवकूफ, नफरत, bakwas, bewakoof, pagal, jhoot, ...). In the first 10, four angry fixtures contained lexicon words and were graded correct by keyword lookup rather than by the model — measuring the lexicon against vocabulary the same author chose. These 15 express anger through finality, withdrawal, cold refusal and sarcasm instead, so the model has to earn the label from tone. Expect them to be harder.

label_rubric.calm: warm or settled; affection, thanks, encouragement, reassurance. Nothing to repair.
label_rubric.neutral: logistics and information. No emotional charge in either direction.
label_rubric.frustrated: irritation aimed at a situation or a repeated lapse. Complains about behaviour or an event.
label_rubric.angry: contempt or a verdict on the person — insults, character judgements, stated dislike, or cold withdrawal from the relationship.
